Full-stack application · spreadsheet migration

Subtrade Daily Log

A shared, validated application that preserves useful spreadsheet patterns while adding controlled editing, source traceability, permissions, and familiar exports.

  • RoleApplication design & development
  • TechnologyReact · TypeScript · Azure SQL
  • ContextProfessional work at Graham

The problem

Workbook-based Daily Logs are familiar and flexible, but teams need a consistent shared view of entries, controlled editing, imports that retain source context, and outputs that still fit existing review practices.

Approach

The original portal explored browser-based daily entry, dashboards, reference data, and invoice exports. A later application expanded this into a multi-project log that reads workbook data without executing macros, retains original documents and source-row coordinates, supports inline edits with version checks, and exports familiar XLSX files.

Key decisions

  • Map workbook columns and business rules into structured data without losing source history.
  • Stage imports before they become shared records.
  • Use site-scoped roles for system administration, local administration, and daily users.
  • Recalculate totals and preserve optimistic-concurrency checks during editing.

What it demonstrates

Modernizing a spreadsheet process without throwing away the review patterns and provenance that users still need.

Publication note

This case combines documented prototypes and workflow evolution. It does not claim a current public production deployment.
